item.title: Butler County 4-H Youth Program Information
item.description:
Butler County 4-H offers hands-on learning activities for youth ages 5-18 under adult mentorship. Project members (ages 8+ in 3rd grade) complete at least one project from 200+ options including food and nutrition, sewing, leadership, STEM, woodworking, health, natural resources, and livestock. Learn more at go.osu.edu/bc4h or contact Erin at simpson-sloan.1@osu.edu. Note: TSD approved for information, not affiliated with TSD.

item.title: PTG Newsletter - Spring 2026 Events
item.description:
The Parent-Teacher Group (PTG) newsletter outlines upcoming events from February through May 2026. Key events include Family Skate Night (2/22), Flower Sale (2/25-3/11), Kid's Night Out (3/6), Conference Meals for Teachers (3/12 & 3/17), Hitching Post Dine to Donate (4/23), Flub's Truck at School (5/1), Teacher Unplug Event (5/7), and Field Day (5/17). The PTG is seeking volunteers, particularly a new treasurer to replace Amber Titus who is moving to Middle School. Board members include President Sarah Landenwitsch, Vice President Brianne Ellison, Secretary Ashley Robertson, and Volunteer Coordinator Carli Compton.

item.title: Understanding Decoding: Reading Skills Resources for Parents
item.description:
Decoding is the foundational reading skill of recognizing letter sounds and blending them together to read words (e.g., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ = cat). Reading Rockets provides age-specific activities for parents to support decoding practice: - Kindergarten: Phonics and decoding activities - First Grade: Phonics and decoding activities - Second Grade: Phonics and decoding activities - Third Grade: Video showing how students use syllables to decode longer words

item.title: LIFES Mentorship Program at Bogan Elementary
item.description:
The LIFES Mentorship Program pairs 1-2 Miami University students with 3-6 elementary students (grades 3rd-5th) for weekly enrichment activities during lunch/recess. The program focuses on building meaningful relationships, fostering personal growth, and supporting academic and leadership development through activities, games, team-building, and conversations. Benefits include trusted mentorship, positive role models, confidence in communication, strong peer friendships, and enhanced academic and life skills. Contact Mrs. Crowder for more information.

item.title: LIFES Mentorship Program Information
item.description:
The LIFES Mentorship Program pairs 1-2 Miami University students with 3-6 elementary students (grades 3-5) in a family-style mentorship format. The program meets weekly during lunch/recess for activities, games, team-building, and conversations to build meaningful relationships and support academic and leadership development. Benefits include trusted mentorship, positive role models, confidence in communication, exciting activities, strong peer friendships, and enhanced academic and life skills. The program aims to empower young students to lead with confidence, purpose, and excitement.

item.title: Mother Son Dance at Kramer Elementary
item.description:
The Mother/Son Luau is on Saturday, January 31, 2026, from 6-8 PM at Kramer Elementary School Gym. Tickets are $10 per person and can be purchased online via Venmo at https://forms.gle/F6LjTsLgHj2WWnMk6 or at the door (cash, check, or Venmo accepted). The event includes snacks, a photo booth, balloons, and dance activities including flossing, freeze dance, break dance, limbo, and a mother-son dance competition starting at 6:30 PM. All Talawanda elementary students can attend with a parent, guardian, or caregiver. Dress code is tropical/luau themed. Advance tickets via Venmo are due by Tuesday, January 27; electronic tickets will be emailed by Thursday, January 29.

item.title: Talawanda Preschool Application Lottery 2026-2027
item.description:
Applications are now open for the Talawanda Preschool lottery for the 2026-2027 school year. Typically developing children will be admitted through a lottery to fill limited spaces. Contact Preschool Coordinator Beth Fuechsl at fuechsle@talawanda.org with questions.

item.title: Head Lice Prevention and Treatment Reminder
item.description:
Parents are reminded to check their children's hair regularly for head lice to help prevent spread at school. If lice or nits are found, begin treatment promptly and notify the school nurse. According to CDC guidelines, students with head lice do not need to be sent home early—they can be treated at the end of the day and return to school after beginning appropriate treatment. Resources available: CDC Head Lice and TSD Head Lice Information.
